title: Palisades (Holtec restart): URGENT - Public Comment Before Decision - Palisades DD41 Emergency Amendment - Docket 50-255 [['E-Mail', 'Letter']]

documents.text:
From:           Justin Poole
To:             Ilka Berrios
Cc:             Brent Ballard; Marlayna Doell
Subject:        FW: URGENT – Public Comment Before Decision – Palisades DD41 Emergency Amendment – Docket 50-255
Date:           Thursday, October 8, 2026 9:04:52 AM
Attachments:    DD41_public Comment -Michigan Safe Energy Future.pdf



These were his comments.

From: Kraig Schultz <kraigschultz@gmail.com>
Sent: Thursday, October 8, 2026 8:19 AM
To: PalisadesRestartProject <PalisadesRestartProject.Resource@nrc.gov>; April Nguyen
<April.Nguyen@nrc.gov>; Justin Poole <Justin.Poole@nrc.gov>
Subject: [External_Sender] URGENT – Public Comment Before Decision – Palisades DD41 Emergency
Amendment – Docket 50-255


To: PalisadesRestartProject@nrc.gov

Dear NRC Palisades Restart Project Staff,

Attached is my public comment opposing expedited approval of Holtec's emergency license
amendment request for recovery of fuel assembly DD41 (ADAMS ML26273A469 and
ML26275A214).

I request that this letter be immediately forwarded to the NRC licensing project
manager, technical reviewers, and decision-makers before any final action on this
amendment.

Please confirm receipt, advise whether the amendment has already been approved, and ensure
that my comments are entered into the official public record for Docket No. 50-255.

Given the time-sensitive nature of this matter, I would appreciate confirmation today.

Thank you.

Kraig Schultz
Environmental Health Advocate
Grand Haven, Michigan

Michigan Safe Energy Future
616-540-7027
 October 8, 2026
U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission
ATTN: Document Control Desk
Washington, DC 20555-0001
Re: Palisades Nuclear Plant, Docket No. 50-255 — Opposition to expedited approval of
DD41 fuel recovery amendment
References: Holtec submissions ML26273A469 (September 30, 2026) and ML26275A214
(October 2, 2026)
Dear NRC Commissioners and Staff:
I urge the NRC not to approve Holtec’s proposed one-time alternative fuel-handling
amendment on an expedited basis without a rigorous, independently verified safety review
and meaningful public scrutiny. The recovery of damaged fuel assembly DD41 may be
necessary, but the urgency of returning Palisades to commercial operation must not dictate
the pace of nuclear safety decisions.
Holtec reports that DD41 tilted after release by the refueling machine during core loading,
damaging its upper tie plate and preventing normal retrieval. Holtec also reports that the
assembly is presently stable, under continuous camera surveillance, and subject to
measures intended to prevent further movement. These statements raise a basic question:
What safety necessity requires emergency authorization now, rather than allowing time for
careful investigation and review?
The proposed operation is not routine. It would use a newly fabricated fuel movement device
and transfer canister, lift and transport the assembly outside the normal underwater transfer
route, and carry the loaded canister through the equipment hatch into the spent fuel pool
building. Holtec acknowledges that this operation departs from assumptions in the plant’s
existing safety analysis.
The NRC’s October 2 questions expose unresolved matters deserving independent
attention. Holtec states that complete loss of canister shielding was removed from the
finalized radiological consequences analysis after a drop analysis deemed that event not
credible. The NRC should publicly explain and independently substantiate the basis for that
exclusion, including the assumed drop heights, orientations, impact surfaces, and potential
common-cause failures.
Holtec also confirms that the proposed heavy-load route passes over the North Tilt Pit,
where spent fuel is stored. The NRC should assess potential damage to stored fuel, pool
structures, and water-retaining boundaries from a credible load drop. I am not claiming that a
drop would necessarily breach the pool or cause a spent fuel fire. I am asking the NRC to
demonstrate, with independent analysis, which severe accident sequences are physically
credible and how they are prevented or mitigated.
These concerns should be evaluated alongside other reported Palisades restart issues,
including an incident involving a worker falling into the reactor vessel and Holtec’s approach
to steam-generator degradation. I request that the NRC verify the facts and circumstances of
those events and assess whether they collectively indicate weaknesses in work planning,
human performance, corrective action, management oversight, or safety culture. These other
 events are concerns requiring verification; the two referenced DD41 filings do not themselves
establish their details or a common cause.
Holtec has substantial experience in nuclear decommissioning and fuel management, but
restarting and operating a commercial nuclear power plant requires a demonstrated
operational safety culture. A significant abnormal event during core loading should trigger
greater scrutiny of operational readiness—not a presumption that the licensee’s own
recovery calculations and timetable are sufficient.
I respectfully request that the NRC:
1. Withhold expedited authorization until the technical basis and need for emergency
processing have been independently evaluated and explained.
2. Require a documented root-cause investigation of the DD41 handling event and a review
of corrective actions before the recovery proceeds.
3. Obtain independent expert review of the lifting device, canister, rigging, load path, drop
analyses, shielding assumptions, and contingency procedures.
4. Specifically evaluate drops over the North Tilt Pit, including consequences for stored fuel
and spent fuel pool structural and water-retention integrity.
5. Disclose the basis for excluding complete shielding loss and explain how fuel integrity,
radiation exposure, and stop-work criteria will be monitored.
6. Review the broader restart safety record and provide a meaningful opportunity for public
participation before authorizing this unusual operation.
Holtec’s September 30 filing invokes emergency processing because delay could postpone
activities needed to restore power operation. That may fit a regulatory category for
emergency amendments, but it does not establish an immediate public safety emergency.
The NRC’s mission is to protect public health and safety, not to preserve a commercial
restart schedule.
When a complex operation goes wrong, the appropriate response is to investigate,
independently verify the recovery plan, and proceed deliberately. Please place this comment
in the public record for Docket No. 50-255 and provide a substantive response to the safety
questions raised.
Respectfully,

Kraig Schultz
Environmental Health Advocate
Michigan Safe Energy Future
Grand Haven, MI 49417
